title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages). G is a quotient of GL(2,Z), typically a profinite quotient, carrying the images of the standard elements eps_0, tau, tau', sigma, rho. G^+ is the image of SL(2,Z), with an exact sequence 1 -> G^+ -> G -> {±1} -> 1. rho has order 6 and sigma has order 4, with rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1. eps_0 is the unipotent cusp generator. Grothendieck defines Z_{rho,sigma} as the set of quadruples (u, mu, eps, eps') in Aut(G^+) x Zhat^* x {±1} x {±1} such that: u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu; u(rho) is G^+-conjugate to rho^{eps'}; u(sigma) is G^+-conjugate to sigma^{-eps}. L_rho = <rho> and L_sigma = <sigma> are quotients of Z/6 and Z/4.

This page.
(9) There is a commutative diagram {±1} -> L_rho ⊂ G^+ and {±1} -> L_sigma ⊂ G^+, with -1 sent to rho^3 = sigma^2. If G is 'big enough', {±1} injects into G^+ (i.e. -1 ≠ 1) and even L_rho ∩ L_sigma = {±1}.
(10) Hence every u from Z_{rho,sigma} sends L_rho and L_sigma to G^+-conjugates of themselves.
Rigidity argument, in three conditions:
- If rho is not G^+-conjugate to rho^{-1}, and sigma not to sigma^{-1}, then the signs eps, eps' are determined by u. So an element of Z is determined by (u, mu); the transcription's '(mu, mu')' is a misreading.
- If the map Zhat -> G^+, n -> eps_0^n, is injective, then mu is determined by u, via u(eps_0) = eps_0^mu.
- So, when G^+ is big enough for all three conditions, the projection Z_{rho,sigma} -> Aut(G^+) is injective. One sufficient condition is a 'modular homomorphism' (12) G -> GL(2,Zhat) sending rho, sigma, tau' to the elements of the same name.

The next page continues: an inner embedding of the cusp group L_0 into Z, the quotient gamma_{rho,sigma} = Z / Im L_0, and characters to mu, eps, eps'.

Purpose. Z_{rho,sigma} (and gamma_{rho,sigma}) is a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group built from the automorphisms of (profinite) SL(2) that respect the cusp and the elliptic torsion classes. This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' around GT and the modular tower at level (1,1).
errors: No mathematical error found. The non-conjugacy hypothesis is genuinely needed and does hold in SL(2,Zhat), though not mod p. In SL(2,F_p), rho and rho^{-1} have the same trace and are conjugate (p > 3). In SL(2,Z_3), conjugacy would require -1 to be a norm of a unit of Z_3[zeta_3]; it is not, since norms of units are ≡ 1 mod 3. Similarly, for sigma in SL(2,Z_2), unit norms from Z_2[i] are ≡ 1 mod 4. So the modular homomorphism (12) indeed forces all three conditions, but the 3-adic and 2-adic components are what make it work. Grothendieck asserts this without proof.
Minor: the injectivity of n -> eps_0^n needs the closed subgroup generated by eps_0 to be ≅ Zhat; this holds in SL(2,Zhat).

ideas.what: Group Z_{rho,sigma} of automorphisms of (profinite) SL2 preserving the cusp generator up to a Zhat^*-power and the torsion classes rho, sigma up to inversion; quotient by cusp-inner automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: GT-type group defined via automorphisms of profinite SL(2,Z)/B_3 (cf. GT ⊂ Out(B_3^hat) / Aut(SL2^hat))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1990s), Nakamura and Minamide–Nakamura for automorphisms of profinite braid/modular groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and SL2-hat in spirit only; this explicit group is in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation

ideas.what: Rigidity: Z_{rho,sigma} -> Aut(G^+) injective once rho !~ rho^{-1}, sigma !~ sigma^{-1}, and eps_0 generates a copy of Zhat; guaranteed by a modular map to GL(2,Zhat)
ideas.modern_name: faithfulness of the cyclotomic/sign characters via local non-conjugacy of elliptic elements

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a GT-like group directly as cusp- and torsion-class-preserving automorphisms of quotients of GL(2,Z), for an arbitrary 'big enough' quotient G, rather than via B_3 or F_2. This anticipates the later SL2-hat / B_3-hat characterisations of GT-type groups (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura). It is an independent unpublished formulation, but the page itself contains only routine set-up.
missed.quote: alors un élément de Z_{rho,sigma} est connu par la seule connaissance de u ∈ Aut(G^+)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents Grothendieck's own route to GT via the modular group with an arbitrary quotient G. That allows finite-level analogues, of interest for the study of GT acting on finite quotients and dessins.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, correct set-up of a GT-type automorphism group of profinite SL2 with routine rigidity remarks. The general idea is known from Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak–Schneps; only the formulation over arbitrary quotients G is mildly distinctive.
transcription_corrections: 'connu par la seule connaissance de (mu, mu')' should read '(u, mu)'.
(11) is 'Zhat -> G^+, n -> eps_0^n', not 'eps sigma^n'.
(12) gloss reads '(transformant rho, sigma, tau' en les éléments de même nom)'.
(9) is drawn as a commutative diagram {±1} -> L_rho ⊂ G^+ and {±1} -> L_sigma ⊂ G^+, with the header 'un diagramme commutatif et des monomorphismes'.
The first 'assez gros' clause reads 'si G est "assez gros", on aura d'ailleurs que {±1} ↪ G^+, i.e. "-1" ≠ 1 dans G^+'.
